messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — Finlytics (enterprise) reporting intermittent 599/timeouts on hosted generate+stream requests; started ~09:20 UTC. They say ~8-12% of streaming requests either return 599 or sit until the client times out. Happening across us-west and us-east. Repro steps below, sharing logs we got. Escalating for triage.

alex_support: Repro steps from customer:
```
# python example using our SDK
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=REDACTED)
for i in range(40):
    c.generate_stream(model=\"redwood-xl-1\", prompt=large_prompt, stream=True)
```
They run ~40 concurrent streams with a ~6k token prompt and see failures after ~200-500 tokens streamed.

alex_support: Customer logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T09:21:05Z] request_id=abcd1234 status=499 client_timeout
[2026-03-17T09:21:06Z] request_id=abcd1240 error=599 detail=\"upstream response closed\"
[2026-03-17T09:21:07Z] request_id=abcd1243 warning=kvcache_lock_wait ms=1200
[2026-03-17T09:21:07Z] request_id=abcd1247 status=502 detail=\"stream reset by upstream\"
```
They see a couple of `kvcache_lock_wait` warnings in the middle of failures.

priya_sre: Thanks Alex. Can you attach the full ingress logs + the edge proxy ids for a couple of failed request_ids? We need the connection IDs to correlate. Also which SDK version is the customer on?

alex_support: SDK v1.12.4 — attached logs in the ticket (internal link). Edge proxy ids for abcd1234/1240/1243 attached in ticket.

jordan_backend: Looking at the paraphrased logs — that `kvcache_lock_wait` line is interesting. We recently changed hot-prefix prefetch in the runtime; suspect a lock amplification under concurrent cold prefixes. Will try to repro on staging with similar concurrency and prompt sizes.

liam_devx: Quick temp mitigations to recommend to customer while we investigate: 1) reduce concurrent streaming connections to 8-10, 2) set SDK keepalive to true and bump keepalive timeout to 90s (helps edge connection reuse), 3) if possible use streaming=false for very large prompts (less sensitive to small stream resets). Share this as a temporary band-aid.

priya_sre: I'll also check edge timeout metrics and connection resets around that timeframe. If the edge is closing idle upstreams we might see stream resets manifesting as 599. Will verify.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-14 — severity=low-med, assigned=jordan_backend, priya_sre.

jordan_backend: Repro attempt on staging: spun up 48 concurrent streaming clients with a 5.5k token prompt. After ~2 minutes we see the same pattern: a subset of connections block while trying to fetch KV cache for early tokens, then their upstream worker resets. Root cause looks like a lock on prefix loads when many concurrent cold requests hit the same model shard. Rapid spike causes queueing. Posting a short log excerpt from staging: 
```
[stg] worker=wu-07 event=kvcache_fetch start key=prefix_0
[stg] worker=wu-03 event=kvcache_fetch start key=prefix_0
[stg] worker=wu-07 event=kvcache_fetch blocked_wait ms=980
[stg] worker=wu-03 event=kvcache_fetch blocked_wait ms=1012
[stg] worker=wu-07 event=upstream_reset reason=\"conn_closed\"
```
Looks like lock contention on prefix_0.

jordan_backend: Plan: (1) change kvcache lock to per-prefix finer-grained lock (cuts head-of-line) — small runtime change, (2) apply canary to dedicated staging pool, (3) monitor p50/p95 for stream reset and kvcache_wait. If canary looks good, roll to prod. ETA for canary today EOD PST.

priya_sre: For immediate prod mitigation we can increase the proxy upstream idle timeout from 45s -> 90s to reduce premature upstream closures while we push patch. I'll coordinate with infra to make a targeted change in us-west first. That should reduce 599/stream resets as a stopgap.

alex_support: I'll tell Finlytics: please try the client mitigations (lower concurrency + keepalive) and we'll update them when the canary is up. Also offer a temporary quota/ingress smoothing if they need it.

liam_devx: Suggested customer message (short): \"We're seeing a transient server-side issue for some streaming requests under high concurrency. Try reducing concurrent streams to ~8–10 or set keepalive until we finish a targeted fix; we expect a mitigation canary today.\"

alex_support: Sent that to customer with :thumbsup:. They asked for ETA; told them tentative \"today EOD PST for canary, 24–48h for full rollout depending on results.\"

ops-bot: Change request opened: CHG-20260317-92 — proxy idle-timeout bump (us-west canary) scheduled in 15m.

jordan_backend: Pushed kvcache lock change to canary branch; running soak on staging now. Logging improved to show per-prefix wait counts. If staging soak looks stable for 1h I'll request canary deploy to us-west prod.

priya_sre: Monitors to watch: edge.stream_resets, runtime.kvcache_wait_ms.p95, ingress.conn_close_by_upstream. I'll post updates in the incident ticket.

alex_support: Customer acknowledged and reduced concurrency for now. Will follow up after canary. Thanks team.

jordan_backend: Quick note — found a small race where two prefixes map to same shard under a rare hashing case; patch also includes a small hash normalization. Deploying to canary now.

priya_sre: Canary to prod-uswest scheduled and running. Initial metrics look promising: stream_resets down ~70% during the canary window.

alex_support: Updated customer: \"We've deployed a targeted canary and initial results look good — significant reduction in stream resets. We'll keep you posted and will backfill any billing anomalies due to retry storms.\" They replied :relieved:.

alex_support: Closing loop for now — will reopen if customer sees regressions. Internal incident INC-20260317-14 will remain open until full rollout and 48h post-rollout monitoring.
